definition.en: The full participation of all persons in education, irrespective of individual prerequisites.

en: It shifts the logic from adapting the individual to the system (integration) towards adapting the system to the diversity of all learners. Inclusion is at once a descriptive concept and a normative, human-rights claim: The concept addresses as well normative human-rights as at the same the system- and the institution. Thus inclusion formulates a goal and a yardstick for the design of educational systems. The concept is normative and action-oriented. Inclusion construes the difference that leads to exclusion as a barrier to participation to be overcome, thereby making relations of power and exclusion an object of pedagogical and policy change. Critical scholarship cautions that "inclusion" can be co-opted unless it confronts the structures that produce exclusion.
